SQL trick that many data professionals 𝐝𝐨𝐧'𝐭 𝐤𝐧𝐨𝐰:
Instead of using CASE WHEN inside aggregate functions, you can simplify your queries using FILTER.
Example:
Imagine you have a sales table:
CREATE TABLE sales (
region VARCHAR(50),
product VARCHAR(50),
revenue DECIMAL(10,2)
);
INSERT INTO sales (region, product, revenue) VALUES
('North', 'Product A', 1000),
('North', 'Product B', 1500),
('South', 'Product A', 2000),
('South', 'Product B', 2500);
𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐀𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐜𝐡 (𝐔𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐖𝐇𝐄𝐍):
SELECT
region,
SUM(𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐖𝐇𝐄𝐍 product = 'Product A' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS product_a_revenue,
SUM(𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐖𝐇𝐄𝐍 product = 'Product B' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS product_b_revenue
FROM sales
GROUP BY region;
𝐎𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐳𝐞𝐝 𝐀𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐜𝐡 (𝐔𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐅𝐈𝐋𝐓𝐄𝐑):
SELECT
region,
SUM(revenue) 𝐅𝐈𝐋𝐓𝐄𝐑 (WHERE product = 'Product A') AS product_a_revenue,
SUM(revenue) 𝐅𝐈𝐋𝐓𝐄𝐑 (WHERE product = 'Product B') AS product_b_revenue
FROM sales
GROUP BY region;
Some SQL Engines such as PostgreSQL and #aws Redshift Optimize FILTER Better than CASE WHEN!
